the angiographic findings during acute hypotensive hypovolemia in the dog are: reduction in caliber of the main renal, segmentary, and interlobular arteries, as well as of main and interlobular veins; prolonged circulation time, suggesting diminished renal blood flow; irregularity of the cortical nephrogram, suggesting redistribution of renal blood flow; and early opacification and filling of the main renal veins, suggesting a change in renal hemodynamics.
the renal angiographic appearance during acute hemorrhagic shock consists of reduction of renal artery diameter and of intrarenal arteries and veins, as well as a prolonged circulation time.
